Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
The bug report describes an issue where resetting the default namespace causes an endless loop in the call to .asPath() on a particular node, specifically when calling this on a 'test' node element which has an empty namespace in a DOM tree with multiple namespace declarations.

Looking at the source code of DOMNodePointer.asPath, it constructs the path string recursively by first calling parent.asPath() then appending the current node's information. In the case of an element node, if the parent pointer is also a DOMNodePointer, it appends the local name and prefix of the current node's namespace URI.

To get the namespace prefix, asPath calls getNamespaceURI() to get the namespace URI of the current node, then asks the NamespaceResolver for the prefix associated with that namespace URI.

The implementation of DOMNodePointer.getNamespaceURI(node) tries to get the namespace URI from the DOM element first; if it is null, it attempts to find the URI by checking for an attribute of the form xmlns or xmlns:prefix on the node and its ancestors.

The potential problem lies in NamespaceResolver.getPrefix(nsURI). If the default namespace was reset to empty ("") on some node, the NamespaceResolver might treat the empty string as a valid namespace URI and try to resolve a prefix, possibly ending up in a recursive loop or returning null improperly.

In the asPath() code, if getPrefix(nsURI) returns null, the code appends "node()[position]" instead of "prefix:localName[position]". This fallback might be correct but if getPrefix(nsURI) calls involve traversing namespaces in the DOM or XPath context and calling asPath() again (due to the NamespaceContextPointer linking back to the node), then an endless recursion occurs.

The key insight is that resetting the default namespace to an empty string or null causes getPrefix to fail to resolve correctly and potentially triggers recursion when asPath tries to compute the prefix via NamespaceResolver, causing the endless loop.

Summary:
- asPath calls getNamespaceURI() and uses NamespaceResolver.getPrefix(uri) to build path segment.
- getNamespaceURI properly returns null or the URI, including checking for empty default namespace.
- getPrefix when namespace is empty or reset may cause recursive calls through NamespaceContextPointer.
- This causes endless recursion in asPath() when attempting to build the path string with prefix.

Hence, the root cause is incorrect or missing handling of the empty default namespace in NamespaceResolver.getPrefix or in the integration of NamespaceResolver with DOMNodePointer, leading to infinite recursion. The recursion is triggered when asPath calls getPrefix for a namespace URI that resolves to the empty default namespace reset on the 'test' node.

The failing test calls doTest("b:foo/test",...) where the 'test' node has a reset default namespace xmlns="" which triggers this code path in asPath causing the infinite loop as described.

Next step would be to inspect NamespaceResolver.getPrefix(String) and its handling of empty or default namespaces especially when the NamespaceContextPointer is set to the DOM node pointer to identify why recursion arises.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
